article_sentences: Climate change increased the damage caused by the tropical Cyclone Arnab, which struck eastern India on October 28, by 33%, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in additional direct economic losses compared to a pre-industrial climate baseline, according to a new study.
It added that the storm brought intense rain, peak 1-minute sustained winds of up to 202 kilometres per hour, and severe damage to infrastructure across Andhra Pradesh.
The study was carried out by researchers at the Imperial College London’s Grantham Institute and published on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

For their analysis, researchers used the Imperial College Storm Model (IRIS) to simulate Cyclone Arnab under current conditions (plus 1.3° Celsius above pre-industrial levels) versus a counterfactual climate without human-induced warming.
“Climate change increased Cyclone Arnab’s maximum wind speed by approximately 5%, and intensified its eyewall rainfall rate by 11% at landfall,” according to the study.

It also revealed that direct damage to physical assets in India was estimated to be 33% higher than it would have been in a pre-industrial climate baseline, attributing roughly 25% of the total economic damage directly to climate change.
In a statement, Dr. Nathan Sparks, researcher at the Department of Physics, Imperial College London, said: “These findings are a powerful reminder of the price of inaction.
The costs of climate change are not hypothetical future projections — they are hitting coastal communities in eastern India today.”

The highest amount of rainfall in Khammam was 13.5 mm in JVR OCP.
I&II, 6.3 mm in Pedapalli and 4.5 mm in Mancherial.

The highest of 235 mm in Mulakapalle of Bhadradri Kothagudem was followed by 204.7 mm in Vemsoor of Khammam, as per Telangana Development Planning Society’s latest weather report issued in the morning on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

stories.headline: How 3D Visual Models Can Make Flood Preparedness Training More Practical in Assam
stories.title: How 3D Visual Models Can Make Flood Preparedness Training More Practical in Assam
stories.summary: Flood preparedness is difficult to teach through instructions alone. A resident may understand a warning in principle but still struggle to picture how rising water could affect the road to a shelter, where medicines should be stored or why one household may need more time to evacuate than another. In Assam, where floods repeatedly disrupt homes, transport and education, preparedness activities need to turn general advice into decisions people can recognise. Simple 3D visual models can support that process by giving students and community members something concrete to examine, question and rearrange. An AI 3D generator can help educators create initial models of objects such as raised houses, relief boats, emergency supply boxes and temporary shelters from written descriptions. Meshy works through a browser and can export generated assets for further editing. The free plan is enough to generate and preview models; downloading them requires a paid plan. These models can support lesson planning and tabletop exercises, but they must not be treated as official maps, engineering designs or predictions of how a real flood will develop. Why Visual Preparedness Exercises Can Help Conventional awareness materials often use posters, maps and lists of instructions. These remain valuable, especially because they are inexpensive to distribute and easy to print. However, they may not show how several decisions are connected. A tabletop scene can make those relationships easier to discuss. Participants might see a cluster of houses, a school on higher ground, a blocked road, a boat landing point and a temporary shelter. The facilitator can then introduce a scenario: heavy rainfall has continued, an official warning has been issued and one route is no longer usable. The group must decide what information it needs, which official instructions to follow and who may require additional assistance. The model does not provide the answer. It creates a shared setting in which people can explain their reasoning. Make the Scenario Local Without Pretending It Is Exact A training model can reflect familiar features such as stilted homes, village roads, embankments, livestock areas or elevated community buildings. Familiarity makes the exercise easier to understand, but the scene should be clearly labelled as illustrative. Using the name of a real village while inventing roads, water depths or shelter locations could cause confusion. If a session refers to actual geography, the relevant information must come from authorised maps and local disaster-management officials. Build the Exercise Around People, Not Objects A preparedness model becomes more useful when participants consider the needs of different residents. A household with young children faces different constraints from one caring for an older person who has limited mobility. Someone who depends on refrigerated medicine may require a plan for maintaining safe storage. Families with livestock also need instructions appropriate to local arrangements. One possible classroom or community exercise could proceed as follows: • Introduce an imaginary settlement and explain that it is not an official risk map. • Assign participants different household situations. • Present an official warning and close one route in the scenario. • Ask each group what information, supplies and assistance it would need. • Compare the decisions with guidance provided by trained facilitators. • Record questions that should be referred to local authorities. • End by identifying the difference between a classroom scenario and a real emergency. This format encourages participation without asking students or untrained residents to make operational decisions beyond their responsibility. Include Communication Breakdowns Flood exercises should not assume that every participant has continuous internet access, a charged phone or the same level of literacy. The facilitator can introduce a power cut, weak mobile coverage or a message available in only one language. Participants can then discuss how verified information might reach households through several channels. The exercise should reinforce the use of official warnings and recognised local communication networks rather than encouraging people to rely on an unverified social media post. Connect Visual Activities to Official Preparedness Guidance The National Disaster Management Authority's community-based disaster risk reduction guidelines frame communities as active participants in preparedness, response, recovery and risk reduction. A 3D exercise can support this approach when it helps residents identify questions, understand responsibilities and practise communication. It cannot replace official hazard assessments, evacuation planning or emergency drills. Water movement depends on rainfall, river conditions, terrain, drainage and infrastructure. A generated visual scene does not calculate any of these factors. The safest approach is to use the model as a discussion aid within a programme led or reviewed by qualified teachers, disaster-management personnel and local authorities. Review Every Model Before It Enters the Classroom AI-generated assets can contain plausible-looking errors. A boat may have an unrealistic hull, a staircase may be unusable, or a shelter may appear structurally sound despite being only a visual interpretation. Before an exercise, the facilitator should inspect the models for misleading details. Objects should be simplified when realism could imply engineering accuracy. Labels, colours and symbols also need review so that they do not conflict with official materials. Separate Visualisation from Engineering A generated model of a raised house may help explain why people protect documents and supplies above expected water levels. It cannot determine the safe height of a real building or verify its foundation. Likewise, a model of a rescue boat may support a discussion about boarding order and essential supplies, but it cannot establish capacity, stability or operational suitability. Those questions require approved equipment specifications and trained personnel. This distinction should be stated at the beginning and end of every exercise. Design for Schools and Low-Resource Settings A useful preparedness activity should not depend on advanced computers. The models can be shown as still images, short rotations or simple videos if an interactive viewer is impractical. Where 3D printing is available, a few durable objects may be printed for repeated classroom use, but printing is optional. Facilitators should also provide text descriptions and high-contrast diagrams. Students with visual, motor or cognitive disabilities may need tactile elements, additional explanation or alternative ways to participate. Language matters as well. Instructions should use terms understood by the intended community, with translations reviewed by local speakers. A technically correct message can still fail if it is unfamiliar, ambiguous or difficult to read. Measure Learning Through Decisions and Questions The quality of an exercise should not be judged by how realistic its models look. A visually polished scene has limited value if participants leave without knowing where official warnings come from or whom to contact. A better evaluation asks whether participants can distinguish verified information from rumours, identify household members who may need assistance, explain why an evacuation order must be followed and name questions that require an official answer. Teachers can repeat the same scenario later with one condition changed. A route may close earlier, the shelter may become unavailable or communication may fail. Comparing the group's responses can reveal whether participants are applying principles rather than memorising one sequence. Frequently Asked Questions Can AI-generated 3D models predict which areas will flood? No. They are visual assets, not hydrological models. Flood forecasts and risk maps must come from authorised agencies using validated data and appropriate scientific methods. Should students design real evacuation routes with these models? Students may discuss hypothetical choices for learning purposes, but actual evacuation routes and shelter locations must be determined and communicated by responsible authorities. Is 3D printing required for this type of activity? No. Models can be displayed on a screen or converted into still images. The teaching objective should determine the format, particularly where devices, electricity or internet access are limited. Use Technology to Strengthen Preparedness Conversations 3D visualisation can make flood-preparedness training more participatory, particularly when abstract instructions are placed within a recognisable scenario. It can help students ask better questions and help facilitators identify misunderstandings before an emergency. Its role must remain carefully defined. Meshy can accelerate the creation of visual assets for a lesson, while local knowledge, official guidance and trained professionals determine what the exercise should teach. The most effective model is therefore not necessarily the most detailed one. It is the model that encourages people to discuss realistic needs, recognise the limits of their information and understand where to obtain trusted instructions when conditions become dangerous. stories.headline: Jaipur celebrates Pia Dandia's election to US House of Representatives from Florida
stories.title: Jaipur celebrates Pia Dandia's election to US House of Representatives from Florida
stories.summary: Indian-American Democrat, whose family hails from Jaipur, defeated Republican Casey Askar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The festive season is witnessing an added celebration in Jaipur's Dandia household after Indian-American Democrat Pia Dandia won election to the US House of Representatives from Florida, defeating Republican candidate Casey Askar in a constituency traditionally dominated by Republicans.
Dandia's victory drew congratulations from Indian-American Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal, who welcomed her as the third South Asian American woman in the House, alongside herself and Aisha Wahab.
"Congratulations to @PiaforCongress for winning her election!
I am so excited to welcome the third South Asian American woman (along with me and @aishabbwahab) to the House!!!" Jayapal wrote on X.
Although born and raised in the United States, Dandia has maintained close links with Jaipur and India since childhood.
Her family gathered at their home near Rambagh Circle Road in Jaipur to celebrate her election.
Dandia is the daughter of Dr Rohit Dandia and Bharati Dandia, and the granddaughter of Dr P C Dandia, a distinguished pharmacologist who is 101 years old.
Dr P C Dandia served as professor emeritus at Sawai Man Singh Medical College in Jaipur, where his son also studied medicine.
Her paternal grandmother, Dr Chandrakanta Dandia, was director of the Department of Adult Education at Rajasthan University.
Her parents moved to the United States around four decades ago.
Dandia grew up with strong connections to her Indian heritage.
Her parents sent her on trips to India as a child to spend time with her cousins in Jaipur.

stories.headline: White House sticks to Trump agenda after midterm election outcome
stories.title: White House sticks to Trump agenda after midterm election outcome
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 5 : The White House has vowed to resist attempts to reverse President Donald Trump's policies during the final two years of his presidency, predicting that Democratic challenges on immigration, taxation, energy and other issues would fail. The White House Office on Wednesday (local time) defended the administration's record and raised the prospect of another impeachment effort, while offering no details of a specific proceeding or legislative proposal. "In the final two years of his presidency, Democrats will try -- and fail -- to reverse everything President Trump has done," the statement said. The release, issued a day after the November 3 midterm elections, portrayed the coming political contest as a defence of Trump's existing policies. It did not announce a new executive action, legislative initiative or negotiating position. "These efforts will fail; the American people have already rejected this agenda," the White House said. The statement placed immigration enforcement prominently among the policies it pledged to defend. It accused Democrats of seeking to undo border restrictions and large-scale deportations, presenting those predictions as part of a broader attack on the opposition. It did not identify specific Democratic bills or statements supporting each of the intentions it attributed to the party. Its descriptions of what Democrats would pursue were the administration's political assertions, rather than an agreed account of the opposition's programme. On the economy, the White House defended Trump's tax cuts and claimed they had delivered record growth. It also credited the administration with record energy production and what it described as American energy independence. The release did not provide figures, time periods or comparisons to substantiate those economic and energy claims. It linked to a separate White House account of Trump's second-term record. Law enforcement was another focus. The statement claimed that Trump had produced the largest decline in violent crime in modern history, but did not include supporting crime statistics or specify the period covered by that comparison. The White House also pledged to defend its actions against diversity, equity and inclusion programmes, commonly known as DEI. It accused Democrats of seeking to restore those programmes and reverse administration policies affecting transgender minors. Other passages alleged that Democrats would rebuild censorship mechanisms and weaken efforts to curb waste, fraud and abuse. The statement did not identify particular measures underpinning those accusations. The White House accused Democrats of wanting to expand the Supreme Court and predicted another attempt to impeach Trump. It did not name lawmakers pursuing those steps or describe a formal proposal. The release characterised the President's earlier impeachment proceedings as failed efforts and said future attempts to reverse his agenda would meet the same outcome. The message was a pledge of continued political resistance: "President Trump will never stop fighting." --IANS

article_sentences: The Chhattisgarh High Court has upheld an Election Tribunal's decision refusing to reject an election petition merely because the election petitioner had not sought recounting of votes during the counting process.
The Court held that specific allegations of discrepancies in vote tabulation and manipulation of election records raised triable issues which required adjudication on evidence.

Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad was hearing a writ petition filed by the returned candidate challenging the Election Tribunal's rejection of his application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, seeking rejection of an election petition.
The election petition had raised a challenge to the election of the petitioner, alleging irregularities in the counting and tabulation of votes at Polling Booth No. 187.

The returned candidate argued that recounting was not sought during the counting process on February 23, 2025, as contemplated under Rule 80(1) read with Rule 80(5) of the Chhattisgarh Panchayat Nirvachan Niyam, 1995.
Relying on Supreme Court decisions, he contended that the election petition was not maintainable in the absence of a request for recounting at the appropriate stage.
The Court noted that while deciding an application under Order VII Rule 11 CPC, the court must examine the election petition as a whole and determine whether its pleadings disclose a cause of action.
The defence raised by the returned candidate and disputed questions requiring evidence cannot ordinarily be considered at this preliminary stage.
The Court observed that the absence of a recounting request during counting did not, by itself, dispense with the requirement of examining the entire election petition.

“The mere fact that no request for recounting was made at the time of counting does not, by itself, dispense with the requirement of examining the entire election petition to determine whether it discloses a cause of action or is ex facie barred by law,” the Court remarked.
The Court further noted that the election petitioner had explained that the discrepancies became apparent only after he obtained the certified tabulation chart.
The Court clarified that it was not deciding whether this explanation was ultimately sufficient or whether the allegations were true; those questions were for the Election Tribunal to determine.

stories.headline: Salman faces backlash over 'Teri Sexy Beauty' song in Maatrubhumi
stories.title: Salman faces backlash over 'Teri Sexy Beauty' song in Maatrubhumi
stories.summary: Mumbai, Nov 5 : Bollywood superstar Salman Khan has found himself at the receiving end of severe criticism on social media after unveiling his latest song, ‘Teri Sexy Beauty’, from his upcoming film Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace. While the actor's return to playback singing after 11 years has grabbed attention, the song has left a section of netizens baffled. Many questioned its relevance in a film based on the 2020 Galwan Valley clash between Indian and Chinese troops. The song, featuring Salman Khan and Chitrangda Singh, was released in the early hours of November 4. Salman also shared a video announcing the track on social media with a rather cheeky caption. "Departure time 5:12 am…. Flight on time , 2 pegs down taking off with my sexy beauty… pata nahi kahaan mai land karoon #TeriSexyBeauty Out Now" The song features Salman crooning alongside Muskaan, with additional vocals by Sajid Khan. It shows Chitrangada Singh in a red saree with Salman also dancing, and the both sharing some romantic and flirtation moments along with a couple of drinks. The song's lyrics and picturisation have not gone down well with a section of the audience, particularly considering the sensitivity of the film's subject. Soon after its release, several X users questioned how a song with lyrics such as "Teri sexy beauty ka fan ban gaya hoon, main do peg pee ke aeroplane ban gaya hoon" could feature in a patriotic film inspired by the sacrifice of Indian Army personnel. One user wrote, "A film based on Col. Santosh Babu & 19 soldiers beaten to death in Galwan and Salman’s tribute is ‘Teri sexy beauty ka fan ho gaya hu, 2 peg peeke talli ho gaya hu.’ How can anyone even think of putting a song like this in a patriotic film. He has zero respect for real martyrs." Another user commented, "Real story pe based patriotic movie me ye sab kya lyrics hai gende. Ek national hero ke character ko kiya bana diya." Another netizen expressed disappointment over the film's changing narrative and musical choices, writing in Hindi that a patriotic film's title, script and songs had seemingly undergone changes. It added that a romantic number now has taken the place of what audiences expected from a film about soldiers. The criticism did not stop there. Many users also took a dig at Salman Khan's singing, with one calling the lyrics "ChatGPT lyrics", while another wrote, "Salmon bhai ruining his own legacy....." A particularly critical user urged the superstar to retire, writing, "Salman Khan, if you don’t want to work properly like you did before 2016, just retire. Please, don’t destroy what’s left of your reputation! Don’t you see, notice, or listen to what you’re actually doing?" Another user sarcastically told the actor, "Bhai. Aap ab bas udd hi jaao," referring to the aeroplane references in the song. However, not everyone was disappointed. Some fans came out in support of Salman, appreciating the catchy tune and his return to singing. For the unversed, Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace which was earlier titled Battle of Galwan, is inspired by the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash, in which 20 Indian Army personnel, including Colonel Bikkumalla Santosh Babu, lost their lives. Salman essays the role of an Army officer, while Chitrangda Singh plays his wife. –IANS

stories.headline: Rupee opens stronger as brent crude drops 1% on Iran hopes
stories.title: Rupee opens stronger as brent crude drops 1% on Iran hopes
stories.summary: Mumbai, Nov 5 : The Indian rupee extended its winning streak for the fifth consecutive session on Thursday, while crude oil prices tumbled as investors bet that the Democrats' sweeping gains in the US midterm elections could push President Donald Trump towards an exit from the Iran war. The rupee opened higher by 29 paise at 94.35 per dollar against Wednesday's close of 94.64. Meanwhile, Brent crude futures fell $1.16 or per cent to $93.46 a barrel extending the decline for a fourth consecutive session. Similarly, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined $1.47 or 1.66 per cent to $86.65. Both benchmarks had tumbled about 10 per cent and settled below $100 per barrel mark in the previous session. Moreover, crude prices have now fallen nearly 16 per cent so far this week. The selloff follows the Democrats' victory in both chambers of Congress, dealing a major setback to Trump and his Republican Party. A Democratic-controlled Congress could constrain the US president's military options and tighten spending on the conflict, giving him a greater incentive to pursue a negotiated exit rather than risk further escalation. Reports claim that a full-scale assault on Iran now appeared less likely. US President Donald Trump also said that Washington had no immediate plans to strike Iran, as per reports. Apart from that, crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz -- the key waterway for most Gulf oil supplies -- have recovered to close to pre-war levels, albeit at a higher cost. The dollar index -- which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies -- fell 0.06 per cent to 101.41 after a 0.36 per cent decline in the prior session. Domestic equity benchmarks also traded higher, jumping nearly 2 per cent each on strong global cues. BSE Sensex opened at 78,910.94, an increase of over 1,600 points or 2 per cent, while the NSE Nifty 50 began trade at 24,378.05, up 417.45 points or 1.74 per cent. --IANS

article_sentences: Two people were killed after a three-storey under-construction building collapsed near Chawri Bazaar in Old Delhi.
Six fire service units were deployed.
Two people were killed after a three-storey under-construction building collapsed in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar area on Thursday morning, police said.
The incident took place in Gali Sattara, Sheesh Mahal, near Chawri Bazaar Metro Station in Chandni Chowk, triggering an emergency rescue operation.
The Delhi Fire Services received a call about the collapse at around 9.50 am.
Multiple emergency teams were rushed to the spot, with six fire service units eventually deployed.
The operation was stepped up after officials received information that people could be trapped beneath the debris.
According to the fire department, the initial response included two water tenders, a water bowser, a Quick Response Vehicle and an Incident Response Team.
Additional personnel and a senior officer were subsequently sent to the location.
The collapse also triggered a political reaction, with Aam Aadmi Party leader Saurabh Bharadwaj questioning the effectiveness of building safety audits in Delhi.
In a post on X, Bharadwaj targeted the Rekha Gupta-led government and the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), asking why buildings continued to collapse despite repeated safety inspections.
He alleged that corruption across government departments had undermined enforcement and claimed that action against buildings was selective.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant requested the High Court to take up the case on a priority basis on November 16.
The Bench allowed Mr. Khan’s counsel, senior advocate Kapil Sibal and advocate Nizam Pasha, liberty to amend the petition to include additional prayers for relief.
The apex court clarified that it has not said anything on the merits of the case.
“The petitioner, Mohd.

Azam Khan, aged about 78 years, a ten-time Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly from Rampur, a former Cabinet Minister and Leader of Opposition in the State of Uttar Pradesh, and a former Member of the Rajya Sabha and of the 17th Lok Sabha, is constrained to approach the Supreme Court… on account of blatant illegality of his arrest including the manner and timing and the gross abuse of process and mala fide exercise of power whereby the machinery of criminal justice system is used for political ends to keep an Opposition leader indefinitely in incarceration particularly on account of the approaching Assembly Elections in the State of Uttar Pradesh,” Mr. Khan’s petition said.

article_sentences: The Court observed that the right to speedy trial, being a fundamental right, cannot be subjected to stringent bail conditions.

The Supreme Court's two-judge bench today expressed reservations about another two-judge bench's judgment in Sukhwinder Singh (2026), which held that the right to speedy trial under Article 21 can't override the stringent statutory requirements for granting bail under Section 37 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1987 (NDPS).

In the verdict pronounced today in Sujit Das v UOI, a bench comprising Justice Ujjal Bhuyan and Justice Atul S Chandurkar expressed that the judgment in State of Punjab v Sukhwinder Singh @ Gora has become "per incuriam" in the light of the 2021 UOI v KA Najeeb judgment, wherein a three-judge bench held that violation of the right to speedy trial is a ground for constitutional Courts to grant bail even under special statutes which provide for stringent bail conditions.
The bench said: "In Sukhwinder Singh alias Gora, this Court observed that the right to speedy trial rooted in Article 21 of the Constitution is undoubtedly a precious constitutional right.

However, the bench proceeded to observe that in matters governed by special enactments such as the NDPS Act, particularly where the recovery is of commercial quantity, the said right under Article 21 must be exercised within the framework of Section 37 and cannot be pressed into service only on the ground of delay to override Section 37."

These fundamental rights cannot be tinkered with so lightly, not even under a special statute."

article_sentences: 96% of Person to Merchant transactions would remain free, the NPCI stated.

Defending its decision to levy charges for transactions above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for Unified Payment Interface (UPI), the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has told the Supreme Court that merchants are barred from passing on MDR charges to customers.
It has further stated that UPI application providers cannot impose platform fees or other charges for UPI payments.

“Second, non-compliance by a Payer PSP or TPAP with the NPCI Circular's directive against passing on MDR to customers constitutes a breach of the binding obligation under the SLAs to abide by all circulars, orders, directions and instructions issued by the Answering Respondent, and exposes such Payer PSP or TPAP to compliance actions which may also lead to termination of its UPI membership and facilities.

Therefore, the non-pass-through directive to the banks and UPI service providers is a mandatory and binding direction, which is enforceable through contractual mechanism in place, and is not a mere 'assurance' or a matter of policy.
Thus, apprehension that the consumers are left exposed to an indirect burden is accordingly without any foundation”, the affidavit states.

NPCI has filed a counter affidavit filed on November 3 in a petition challenging the amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, introduced through the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026, the subsequent Ministry of Finance notification and the revised MDR framework announced in September.

The Supreme Court had in September 2026 sought an affidavit explaining the basis for the move to levy charges for transactions through Unified Payment Interface (UPI) above ₹2,000 from individuals to merchants.

NPCI has submitted that around 96% of person-to-merchant transactions will remain unaffected by the revised MDR, the NPCI has refuted the apprehension that the MDR charges would cause merchants to increase prices.

“The charge under the MDR is attracted only to a small fraction i.e. approximately 4%, of P2M transactions that exceed INR 2,000 and thus, a measure confined so narrowly in its incidence affords less scope for merchants to recalibrate their pricing across their entire customer base merely on account of a charge that arises only occasionally and only above a defined value.
Accordingly, the apprehension that the MDR Framework will result in quiet revision of prices is also misconceived”, the NPCI has stated.
NPCI has stated that person-to-person transactions and transactions involving small merchants under the P2PM category will continue to remain free.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has ruled that the 24-hour deadline for producing an arrested person before a magistrate begins from the moment their liberty is curtailed, and not from the time the police formally record the arrest.
A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that excluding the period of detention before a formal arrest from the 24-hour deadline would violate Article 22(2) of the Constitution.
The ruling came in appeals filed by four people challenging the Tripura High Court's rejection of their bail pleas in a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.
The four accused were detained on September 29, 2025, at around 2 pm during a search and seizure operation.
However, the police formally recorded their arrest only at 11 am the following day.
The Supreme Court held that they should have been produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of their detention on September 29.
According to a LiveLaw report, the court found that the accused had been kept in custody for around 18 hours without judicial oversight, violating their constitutional rights.
It consequently ordered their immediate release.
"Article 22(2) does not sanction exclusion of the time taken for inquiry or investigation before the arresting authority could effect arrest of the detainee," the bench observed.
The court clarified that the only period that can be excluded while calculating the 24-hour deadline is the time required to travel from the place of arrest to the magistrate's court.
It rejected the argument that detention before a formal arrest should be treated differently, observing that fundamental rights cannot be temporarily suspended during an investigation.

The bench also disapproved of earlier rulings by the Orissa High Court in Aryaman Pattanaik, the Kerala High Court in Arun K Thomas and the Madras High Court in Kannan, which had allowed pre-arrest detention to be excluded from the 24-hour calculation.

article_sentences: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday accused the BJP of attempting to wrest control of Maharashtra’s Gokul milk union by changing the cooperative law after the Congress-led panel secured a narrow majority in its board election.

The criticism followed the Maharashtra cabinet’s approval on Wednesday of an amendment allowing the government to appoint five directors, four with voting rights, to certain large cooperative societies receiving state assistance.
At the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul, the Congress-led panel headed by Satej Patil won 13 of the 25 elected seats on 19 October.
The BJP-led Mahayuti panel secured 12.
The proposed appointments could change that balance ahead of the chairman’s election scheduled for 10 November under a Bombay High Court direction.
If all four voting nominees support the Mahayuti-backed directors, their combined strength would rise to 16 against the Congress-led panel’s 13.
Rahul Gandhi described the proposal as an attempt to reverse the verdict delivered by milk producers.
“This is theft of the milk producers’ votes — adulteration in the mandate,” he wrote on X.
He accused the BJP of changing the rules after losing the election and warned that farmers would remember the move.
The cabinet, chaired by chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, approved a proposal to amend Section 73AA(2) of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, through an ordinance.
The provision would apply to cooperative societies with an annual turnover exceeding Rs 500 crore that receive government assistance in the form of funds, land, loans or guarantees.
District Central Cooperative Banks would be exempt.

stories.title: Supreme Court declines to intervene; refers Kalady students' exam plea to Kerala High Court Single Bench
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has declined to intervene in the petition filed by 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady, challenging a Kerala High Court Division Bench order that barred them from appearing for their semester examinations.
The matter has been redirected to the Kerala High Court Single Bench, which has been asked to consider it urgently.
The students had approached the Supreme Court seeking restoration of an interim order passed by a Single Judge on October 30.
The order had allowed them to appear for semester examinations, which began on November 4, subject to the final outcome of their petition challenging their suspension from the university.
The Kerala High Court Division Bench subsequently overturned the interim order, prompting the students to move the Supreme Court.
They had sought permission to provisionally appear for the remaining examination papers and requested special examinations for any papers they might miss before the matter was decided.
The petitioners argued that the Division Bench's decision, delivered on the eve of the examinations, would result in the loss of an entire academic semester.
The 16 students, who are pursuing MSW, MFA, MA, Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) and PhD courses, were suspended by the university on September 1, 2026.
The suspension was pending an inquiry into incidents allegedly linked to a student protest held on the campus on August 13.
